heard: NASA was already 40, three years old before its first launch. In 1957, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, triggering a wave of American panic. The U.S. response was a disaster. The Vanguard rocket exploded on live television. To fix the mess, President Eisenhower signed the 1958 Space Act to create a civilian agency. He rebranded the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics, a research group founded in 1915. NASA opened that October with 8,000 inherited employees and three massive laboratories. Early success relied on former Nazi scientist Wernher von Braun, who developed the V-2 rocket. His team launched Explorer 1 in 1958, turning a 43-year-old committee into a space titan.
